name: Hunting with YARA — Windows Disk, Process Memory, ETW & Linux Memory Images
description: YARA-based threat hunting across all surfaces. Windows disk: yara64.exe -s rule.yar C:\dir -r 2>nul (-s shows matching strings, -r recursive, 2>nul suppresses permission errors). Windows process memory: Get-Process | ForEach-Object { yara64.exe rule.yar $_.id } or yara64.exe rule.yar <PID> --print-strings. ETW live telemetry: SilkETW.exe -t user -pn Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell -ot file -p out.json -y C:\Rules\yara -yo Matches. Linux memory image: yara rule.yar dump.raw --print-strings. Volatility: vol.py -f memory.raw yarascan -y rule.yar.
source: CDSA Module 12: YARA & Sigma for SOC Analysts
notes:
=== HUNTING WITH YARA ON WINDOWS — DISK ===

Scan a directory (recursive), show matched strings, suppress errors:
  yara64.exe -s rule.yar C:\Windows\Temp\ -r 2>nul
  yara64.exe -s rule.yar C:\Users\ -r 2>nul
  yara64.exe -s rule.yar C:\Samples\YARASigma\ -r 2>nul

Flags:
  -s / --print-strings     → print the matched strings and offsets
  -r / --recursive         → scan subdirectories recursively
  2>nul                    → redirect stderr to nul (suppress access-denied errors)

Scan single file:
  yara64.exe -s rule.yar C:\Samples\YARASigma\shell.exe

Scan with multiple rule files:
  yara64.exe -s rules1.yar rules2.yar C:\Samples\ -r 2>nul

Output format:
  RuleName  matched_file_path
  0x14d8:$s1: 45.33.32.156    ← offset : variable : matched value

=== HUNTING WITH YARA ON WINDOWS — PROCESS MEMORY ===

Scan all running processes (PowerShell loop):
  Get-Process | ForEach-Object { yara64.exe rule.yar $_.Id 2>$null }

Scan specific PID:
  yara64.exe rule.yar 1234
  yara64.exe rule.yar 1234 --print-strings

Get PID of a process:
  Get-Process -Name notepad | Select-Object Id
  (or: tasklist | findstr notepad)

Common use cases:
  → Hunt for injected shellcode in process memory
  → Detect in-memory malware that never touches disk
  → Find C2 strings loaded in memory
  → Detect process hollowing artifacts

Note: requires elevated privileges (Admin/SYSTEM) to scan other processes.
Note on output: matched process shows rule name + PID.
  If no match: no output for that PID.

=== ETW (Event Tracing for Windows) WITH SilkETW ===

SilkETW: C# tool that taps ETW providers for live telemetry + YARA scanning.

Hunt PowerShell events in real-time with YARA:
  SilkETW.exe -t user -pn Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell -ot file -p C:\Logs\etw.json -y C:\Rules\yara -yo Matches

Flags:
  -t user              → user-mode ETW session (vs -t kernel)
  -pn <ProviderName>   → ETW provider name (e.g., Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell)
  -ot file             → output type: file
  -p <path>            → output file path (.json)
  -y <path>            → path to YARA rules file or directory
  -yo Matches          → only output events where YARA matched

Other useful ETW providers:
  Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Process     → process creation/termination
  Microsoft-Windows-DNS-Client         → DNS queries
  Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing  → security events
  Microsoft-Antimalware-Service        → Defender events

Output: JSON file with ETW event data + YARA match results

=== HUNTING WITH YARA ON LINUX — MEMORY IMAGE ===

Scan a raw memory dump file:
  yara rule.yar /home/htb-student/memory.raw --print-strings
  yara -s rule.yar /opt/dumps/memory.raw

With multiple rules:
  yara /home/htb-student/rules/*.yar /home/htb-student/memory.raw

With offset/size limits (scan first 1GB only):
  yara rule.yar /home/htb-student/memory.raw --scan-limit=1073741824

Output shows:
  RuleName → hit in memory image
  0x1234567:$s1: matched string value

=== VOLATILITY YARASCAN PLUGIN ===

Basic yarascan with inline string pattern:
  vol.py -f /home/htb-student/memory.raw yarascan -U "pattern_to_find"
  vol.py -f /home/htb-student/memory.raw yarascan -U "iuqerfsodp9ifjaposdfjhgosurijfaewrwergwea.com"

Yarascan with YARA rule file:
  vol.py -f /home/htb-student/memory.raw yarascan -y /home/htb-student/rule.yar

Print matching strings:
  vol.py -f /home/htb-student/memory.raw yarascan -y rule.yar --print-strings

Yarascan flags:
  -U <string>   → scan for literal string
  -y <file>     → use YARA rule file
  -A <addr>     → start scan at virtual address
  -V <string>   → scan for regex pattern

Filter results by process:
  vol.py -f memory.raw --pid 1234 yarascan -y rule.yar

Volatility 3 syntax:
  python3 vol.py -f memory.raw windows.vadyarascan --yara-file rule.yar
  python3 vol.py -f memory.raw windows.vadyarascan --yara-string "evil_string"

=== ONLINE YARA HUNTING ===
Unpac.Me: https://www.unpac.me/#/
  → Upload suspect sample → automatic unpacking
  → Navigate to 'YARA Hunt' section
  → Submit custom YARA rule
  → Hunts against their malware sample database
  → Returns list of matching samples with SHA256 hashes
  → Useful for: testing rule quality, finding more samples of same family

VirusTotal:
  → Supports YARA search via VT Intelligence (paid tier)
  → Retrohunt: run YARA against entire VT corpus
  → Livehunt: run YARA against new submissions in real-time

=== WORKFLOW: COMPLETE YARA HUNT LIFECYCLE ===
1. Analyze initial sample → identify unique strings/bytes
2. Write YARA rule (strings + condition)
3. Test rule:
   → yara rule.yar /path/to/known_malware → expect match
   → yara rule.yar /path/to/clean_files → expect 0 matches
4. Hunt on disk:
   → yara64.exe -s rule.yar C:\ -r 2>nul
5. Hunt in process memory:
   → Get-Process | ForEach-Object { yara64.exe rule.yar $_.Id 2>$null }
6. Hunt in memory image (forensics):
   → vol.py -f memory.raw yarascan -y rule.yar
7. Hunt online:
   → Submit to Unpac.Me YARA Hunt or VT Retrohunt
8. Refine rule based on false positives found
